recipes.name: Easy Homemade Pizza Sauce
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Mix together water, tomato paste, and olive oil in a large bowl or jar. Add garlic, oregano, basil, rosemary, salt, and pepper; mix well.
For best results, let sauce stand for several hours to allow the flavors to blend. No cooking is necessary; just spread on pizza crust.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Homemade Pizza Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This pizza sauce is a simple, no-cook recipe made with just 6 ingredients: tomato paste, olive oil, garlic, oregano, basil, and rosemary.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Homemade Pizza Sauce

review.reviewBody: This is a very good sauce. I have tried quite a few and this is my husband’s favorite. I cut the water amount in half because of others recommendations, I highly recommend this or the sauce will be very thin and watery. I also add a ½ teaspoon of sugar. We make this now once a week!

Easy, yes but way too watery if you follow the recipe. I adjusted the water down to 2/3 cup and replaced the oil with 2 Tbsp. of wine. I added a little salt and 1 tsp. of sugar along with a 1/4 tsp. of onion powder and cut back on the oregano, basil and rosemary to taste using a little over 1/4 tsp. each. Overall, not bad but don't use all that water unless you want a very, very thin sauce.

I am only giving it three stars because I had to tweak it quite a bit. As others suggested I cut the water in half, I'm so glad I did because it would have been super runny. I also reduced the olive oil to 1/4 a cup and added an extra garlic clove. Then, I threw it all in a blender which worked really well. After all these adjustments I can say that my whole family really enjoyed the sauce, my husband especially :)

My father always made this sauce with beer instead of water. I like Budweiser beer for this sauce. It adds just a touch of flavor. I think it helps mellow out the acidic tang of the tomato paste and adds just a bit of sweetness to the flavor. I use the olive oil as noted in the recipe and stir in the beer last to get the sauce to the right viscosity. 

It's going to firm up in the refrigerator, so you'll need to add enough beer so that's it's saucy when you put it in. It will be more like a paste when you take it out. It really should sit for a day to set up, but I have found that a minimum of 6 hours in the refrigerator will get the sauce to a reasonable flavor level. Time is always your friend with tomato/garlic combinations.

This recipe is very good, there's place for making it your own, that's what I like about it, it makes a very good basic. I caramelise 1/2 cup of onions with the olive oil, then I add the garlic cloves, cut in slices. I add a can of whole peeled or diced tomatoes and then I mix the rest in it, I also add a bit of sugar just to break the acid from the tomatoes. Then I blend it a bit, so it stays chunky and you can't see the onions. Delicious, everybody wants more, this is a hit...

This sauce is pretty good, but I made two minor changes. I have a habit of adding citrus juices to anything heavy on tomatoe, as it slightly alters the flavor, so take out about half a cup of water, and add half a cup of orange juice, or another citrus juice. Then, after mixing it all, let it simmer for about an hour. Delicious
Very good sauce. I added 1.5 teasponns of sugar to cut acidity and I simmered the sauce for about 30 minutes while I preparded the toppings and the dough.

This recipe was very tasty with my few changes of NO oil at all, I used 1/2 cup of veggie broth in place of some water, and bc I feel the spices needed to be bloomed to bring out the flavors into the sauce, I put it on the stove at very slow temp for a while. I didn’t time it but maybe 15-20 minutes. You can always add a bit more liquid if it gets a bit thick.

Loved the flavor on this. I used only a cup of water. 1/3 tsp of salt and pepper and used dried garlic instead of fresh and a little dried onion (maybe 1/8 tsp). I used a mortar for the basil, rosemary and oregano- they all have better flavor when you do that. Also I just put the ingredients in tall glass and used an immersion blender to mix. Used immediately and we enjoyed the flavor.

Been looking for a good sauce recipe and excited to have found this! Per another review I halved the water and added 1/2 tsp. of sugar. I didn’t include the rosemary and used fresh basil instead of dried. Because I love amounts when something says “salt and pepper to taste” I used 1/4 tsp. Pepper and 3/8 tsp. Salt.
Followed directions as written, even added 1 Tbs of balsamic vinegar😊 Not watery at all. Maybe their tomato paste was not thick enough? Great recipe for my homemade calzones!
Super easy!!
Added a dash of anise

Ill give 2.5 stars but there is no half star. Used this recipe only cause I had only tomato paste and not any canned crushed tomatos or fresh tomato. Definitely the tomato paste still too prevalent in this recipe. Even though we are trying make tomato sauce when you are using only paste you actually don't want really taste the tomato in my opinion cause paste is strong and nasty. I think it definitely needs some type of sugar, probably a cream, or condensed milk, or just lessen the water and put lil milk and normal sugar or savory addition like honey bbq. Adding any one of those will likely make it better
This is absolutely the worse pizza Sause I've ever tasted in my life, it feels like its missing 50 ingredients.
So easy and so delicious. Thanks for the great recipe!

I don’t understand the people saying this is too watery. I used less than the recommended 1 cup of water to start with, and added a little at a time, due to the warnings, but ended up using the full cup in the end. Maybe some people accidentally used tomato SAUCE instead of tomato PASTE? I’m not sure what happened, but mine came out a nice thick, but not too thick, consistency. I did use a little less than the recommended amount of olive oil, though I still used a pretty generous amount. I added some crushed red pepper because I like everything to have a little kick. Thanks for the simple recipe! I’m glad that I don’t have to spend money buying premade jars of pizza sauce anymore. This was so quick and easy!

This recipe ends up tasting just like tomato paste and olive oil, even with extra spices and water and sugar. Honestly with the amount of corrections that you have to make, it shouldn’t even be a recipe. It literally doesn’t taste good at all. I am leaving the review to warn other people DO NOT use this recipe if you care about what your food tastes like!

We went and continue to go with reduced amounts of EVOO, folks. The first time we made it, we put the recommended amount of oil in it. It was oil-forward in flavor, which is NOT desired in a pizza sauce. Now we do it slowly, not really sure about the actual amounts. We put in garlic powder, Italian seasoning, parmesan, and essentially added the spices as needed, with three tablespoons of water to help with spread/consistency on our pizzas.

Really like this sauce ! It’s super easy. I used garlic powder instead of fresh. Only added 1/2 can of water, from the tomato paste) it needed more. Added more water for 2nd pizza. I think 6 oz might be perfect. I used more herbs and added thyme. I’m making it again for another pizza night. Love it.
